entries.claim: The prescribed BEFORE measurement command trusts every nonblank `reads.jsonl` line as valid JSON, so a truncated or malformed recorder line aborts the entire measurement.
entries.failure_scenario: If `.planning/reads.jsonl` ends with a partially written line (for example `{"agent_id":"x"` after interruption), `JSON.parse(l)` throws. There is no per-line recovery, so the command produces no before figure even though all prior recorder rows and transcripts are usable. This is particularly likely for a JSONL file written by hooks.

counter_evidence.note: The cited lines are a one-off measurement command printed inside a spike document for a human to paste, not code Cadence ships or calls. Cadence has no runtime parser here. A throw on a truncated recorder line fails the measurement loudly and produces no figure; skipping unparseable lines would emit a before-figure that is silently short by however many rows it skipped, which is the worse outcome for a document whose entire purpose is a trustworthy number the after-side is compared against.

entries.claim: The BEFORE measurement command reads the complete recorder into one UTF-8 string with no size cap or streaming path.
entries.failure_scenario: A large or hostile `.planning/reads.jsonl` causes `readFileSync(..., "utf8")` followed by `split` to retain the entire file plus an array of every line. Running the documented command on an oversized recorder can exhaust memory and fail before it reports the measurement.

counter_evidence.note: Same one-off documented command as finding 0, run by hand over .planning/reads.jsonl, which is this repository own read recorder written by its own hooks. There is no untrusted producer and no adversary: the operator owns the file and the machine. A streaming rewrite of a command a human pastes once to produce one number is an approach preference, which the reviewer brief excludes from findings.

entries.claim: The new cache-fact join key concatenates unescaped untrusted `corr` and `agent_id` fields with a NUL delimiter, so distinct pairs can collide and cache figures can be folded onto the wrong bracket.
entries.failure_scenario: A valid hostile JSONL fact with `corr: "run"` and `agent_id: "worker\u0000target"` produces the same map key as an existing bracket with `corr: "run\u0000worker"` and `agent_id: "target"`: both serialize as `run\u0000worker\u0000target`. The post-pass then treats the fact as belonging to that bracket and silently adds its cache totals to the victim. JSON permits escaped NULs, and neither this collection path nor the matching path rejects them.

counter_evidence.note: The NUL-joined composite key is this file pre-existing convention, unchanged by this diff: line 811 builds the worker key as key(corr) NUL key(phase) NUL key(plan) and predates the range. The property is real but the precondition is not reachable through any interface Cadence exposes. corr is machine-derived as phase-sha by planning.mjs and never user text; agent_id arrives through argv on trace close, and argv cannot carry a NUL byte. The only producer is a hand-edited .planning/trace.jsonl carrying an escaped u0000, and that file is gitignored and local, so an author who can write it can write the brackets rows directly and needs no collision. Consequence if reached is a cache figure folded onto the wrong bracket in an advisory render: no crash, no data loss, no privilege boundary. Downgraded from high to low and sent to open items rather than fixed at this gate.
